newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai property bonds approval cautiously welcomed.
newsitem.headline: Thai property bonds approval cautiously welcomed.

text.p: The Thai government's approval on Tuesday of proposals to issue 100 billion baht in zero coupon bonds to support the ailing property sector was cautiously welcomed by analysts on Tuesday.

"It's an interesting idea. We are still a little cautious because it is still not clear as to the extent of the problems in the sector but as an initiative it's a step forward," said James Marshall, head of research at Capital Nomura.
"It's hard to say whether this is a solution. One of the big uncertainties is the lack of disclosure," Marshall said.
The stock market leapt 2.26 percent late on Tuesday as investors welcomed the news and bought shares across the board, brokers said. The index rose 15.86 points to 719.18.

In an statement issued on Tuesday the Thai cabinet said it had approved the establishment of the Property Loan Management Organisation to purchase asset-backed property loans from financial institutions.
The new company would be funded by an issue of the seven-year zero coupon bonds.
The 100 billion baht sum would be sufficient to be of immediate benefit in addressing at least the loan problems of ailing finance firms, analysts said.
The firms have an average of 25 percent of their loans in the property sector, and are faced with a liquidity crunch as the property market has deteriorated.
